questions.question: Explain the routing system: the two questions that send any transaction to its journal, and why receipts from debtors and payments to creditors never touch the Sales or Trading Stock columns.
questions.expected_answer: Ask whether money moved and in which direction; if no money moved, ask what happened (goods on trust out/in, goods back, or an exception for the GJ). Receipts from debtors settle a debt whose sale was already recorded in the DJ, so they strike Bank and Debtors Control only; payments to creditors settle purchases already recorded in the CJ, so they strike Bank and Creditors Control only.

questions.question: Describe the three layers of proof that closed the combined month, and what each layer can catch that the others cannot.
questions.expected_answer: Each journal cross-casts before posting (catching errors inside a journal); both control accounts are compared with their lists (catching detail-versus-summary errors per street); and the trial balance levels at R32 500 (catching arithmetic double-entry failures across the whole ledger). Wrong-account-right-side errors escape the trial balance but can surface in the reconciliations, and vice versa.

questions.question: In your own words, describe the owner's Friday walk and how each stop pairs a physical check with a record.
questions.expected_answer: Till counted against the day's analysis column, then banked intact; shelf sample counted against the Trading Stock balance's claim; debtors list read for limits and ageing debts; supplier statements agreed to their pages with payments scheduled on terms. Every stop tests reality against a record — control is only possible because the books exist.
